title: Base case of the well-ordered union projective resolution argument
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, M an R-module, E a linearly ordered well-ordered set, and F : E → Submodule R M a monotone family with every element of M in some F e. Let U e be the supremum of stages F i with i < e, pulled back into F e. If every quotient F e / U e has a projective resolution of length at most zero [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], then M has one of length at most zero.

proof.text: For each stage e put U_e equal to the predecessor supremum pulled back into F e, and Q_e = F e / U_e. Unpack its length-zero projective resolution. Since its degree-one object is zero, its differential into degree zero is zero. The augmentation is a colimit cokernel cofork, hence an isomorphism by CokernelCofork.IsColimit.isIso_π. Transfer projectivity of degree zero along this isomorphism using Projective.of_iso. The quotient map is epi by ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective and Submodule.mkQ_surjective. Apply categorical Projective.factors to its identity to obtain a section s_e. Choice is confined to the theorem proof. Define ψ by DirectSum.toModule on the section maps followed by stage inclusions.

proof.text: Prove injectivity by Finset.induction_on_max on a finite relation among section images. For an inserted greatest index e, all other summands lie in the predecessor supremum and, by monotonicity, in F e. The relation implies s_e(x_e) equals the negative of their sum, so s_e(x_e) belongs to U_e. Applying its quotient projection and using the section identity gives x_e = 0. The remaining relation is handled by induction. Apply this result to the DFinsupp support of a vector in the kernel of ψ; coefficients outside the support are zero as well, hence the vector is zero.

proof.text: Prove F e ≤ range ψ by well-founded induction on e. Given y in F e, subtract the section of its quotient class. The quotient of this difference is zero, so the difference belongs to the predecessor supremum. Each earlier stage lies in range ψ by induction; iSup_le therefore places the whole predecessor supremum in range ψ. The section term is the image of DirectSum.lof. Add the two terms to get y in range ψ. Finally hcover makes ψ surjective. This formulation avoids the separate identification of a directed supremum with its union and works at a least stage without a separate case.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0D1U (lemma-colimit-projective-dimension, line 26800), proof, lines 26818-26824

proof.text: Use LinearEquiv.ofBijective to identify the external direct sum with M. Prove categorical projectivity of M directly: for a map f from M across an epimorphism p, lift each f composed with a section inclusion using categorical projectivity of Q_e. DirectSum.toModule sums these lifts into χ. DirectSum.linearMap_ext and the component lift identities show p.hom.comp χ = f.hom.comp ψ. Compose χ with the inverse linear equivalence to get the required lift from M. The external sum is never made into a ModuleCat object, so no shrinking or Small R hypothesis is needed. Finally ProjectiveResolution.self M, with its positive-degree terms zero, gives the required length-zero resolution.

theorem hasProjectiveResolutionLE_of_wellOrderedUnion_zero
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (M : ModuleCat.{v} R)
    {E : Type w} [LinearOrder E] [IsWellOrder E (· < ·)]
    (F : E → Submodule R M) (hF : Monotone F)
    (hcover : ∀ x : M, ∃ e : E, x ∈ F e)
    (hquot : ∀ e : E, HasProjectiveResolutionLE
      (ModuleCat.of R ((F e) ⧸
        ((⨆ e' : {i : E // i < e}, F e'.val).comap (F e).subtype))) 0) :
    HasProjectiveResolutionLE M 0
